stemMarkdown: What is the maximum possible number of people who like exactly one of the two drinks?
solutionMarkdown:
Exactly-one equals $130 + 110 - 2 \times (\text{both})$, so it is largest when the overlap is smallest. The smallest possible overlap is 40:

$130 + 110 - 2 \times 40 = 240 - 80 = 160$

**160 people**. That case has nobody outside both circles: 40 like both, 90 like tea only, 70 like coffee only, and $40 + 90 + 70 = 200$. Note the overlap is subtracted **twice** here, once from each group, because someone who likes both is excluded from exactly-one on two counts.
